The v2 publication source wording_status is faithful paraphrase. Its attribution and actual restatement explicitly say that local germs and arbitrary finite real Hilbert spaces including dimensions zero and one are canonical extensions of the book. The lesson retains the descriptive wording_status attributed canonical local generalization while its mathematical source scope and assumptions are unchanged. These two wording labels do not erase the explicit mathematical generalization. This review certifies mathematical/source fidelity, not a repository JSON-enum gate.

Direct inspection of the pinned HFT page images establishes: printed1/PDF9 sets open Omega and standing n>1; printed2/PDF10 defines Ck(Omega); printed13/PDF21 gives Eq1.19 and expressly states real-valued twice continuously differentiable functions. The source is C2 on its open domain. It is not represented as requiring global C2 on all E. The pinned PDF raw digest was verified again against 4e64124f7e36993ee784e575a024505f99d484ccf959d2d3864eae9232af8bf1.

The whole current module was reviewed through the v2 embedded source, equal to the current file. directional_second differentiates evaluation of fderiv. second_product establishes the first product derivative on a neighborhood through ContDiffAt.eventually, transfers derivatives through EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, and differentiates actual product/add derivative maps. This avoids differentiating an equality known only at one point. No global ContDiff hypothesis is introduced.

The public proof uses actual Mathlib canonical-covariant-tensor Laplacian and its orthonormal trace identity, then actual Riesz gradients and Parseval. The resulting cross coefficient is exactly 2. The public signature has only NormedAddCommGroup, real InnerProductSpace and FiniteDimensional structures and local C2 at the same x. The standard basis indexed by Fin(finrank R E) handles empty and singleton bases without a positive-dimension premise.

The actual literal quotient consumer was read again: hne follows internally from norm(x)<1 and norm(zeta)=1; the numerator norm-square polynomial is smooth; the denominator inverse norm power is locally smooth by x-zeta nonzero. div_eq_mul_inv exposes exactly P(z)=(1-norm(z)^2)/norm(z-zeta)^n. The conclusion retains three unevaluated derivative terms, so it establishes product expansion only, not harmonicity or a numerical integral.

The existing compact graph consumer specializes its already globally smooth theta and r_n to ContDiffAt 2 at each point. Its ordinary-volume graph conclusion is not strengthened. The actual same-D/same-u/all-cutoffs conditional consumer boundary remains separate from weighted-domain/core and PBPS/SPHMC main results.

Printed14/PDF22 exhibits two alternative normalization proof routes, while printed15/PDF23 uses harmonicity, continuity and maximum principle for representation. The raw pinned paper A1 section uses both h=1 and h=x1 and division by positive 1-r^2, and retains its raw n>=2/trailing n>=3 wording. The source-only graph is only an index to regions and AND/OR boundaries, not an accepted verdict. Product calculus closes none of those downstream claims.

reader_review.assumptions_review: All three assumption paragraphs match the actual real finite-Hilbert local-C2 contract, explicitly separate open-domain n>1 source scope from canonical E0/E1 generalization, and identify actual Riesz/canonical-tensor operators.
reader_review.formula_review: The main three-line formula is the exact product identity at x; directional derivative, gradient and finite trace notation agrees with actual definitions. The literal Poisson notation includes pole separation and does not claim Laplacian zero or normalized integral.

steps.title: Differentiate the product twice locally
steps.formula_review: D_v^2(fg)=f D_v^2g+2D_vf D_vg+g D_v^2f is correct at x under both local C2 assumptions.
steps.evidence: second_product uses ContDiffAt.eventually for the nearby first product derivative, EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq for differentiating the germ equality, actual HasFDerivAt.mul/add, and directional_second for evaluation of D(Df).

steps.title: Take the orthonormal trace
steps.formula_review: Summing diagonal second derivatives gives f Delta g plus twice the derivative-pairing sum plus g Delta f.
steps.evidence: ht uses Mathlib laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_stdOrthonormalBasis and iteratedFDeriv_two_apply. Finset.sum_add_distrib and mul_sum extract the coefficients independent of the index.

steps.title: Identify the gradient pairing
steps.formula_review: The sum of directional derivative products equals the real inner product of actual gradients.
steps.evidence: hi uses stdOrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner and inner_gradient_left/right; real conjugation is trivial. Empty and singleton bases respectively cover E0 and E1, with no Nontrivial premise.

reader_review.boundary_review: Local calculus identity only. Genuine quotient and compact-graph reuse are present, but kernel harmonicity, mean-value/sphere normalization, both A1 numerical identities, Eq24, TV/oracle/query/cost/main lower bounds, weighted core and PBPS/SPHMC completion remain separate. No AND of alternative normalization routes or OR of the two required A1 values is introduced.
